headline: Across media, gaming, publishing and education, revenue trends are mixed while tech spend varies between expansion and tightening.
summary: Media & Entertainment shows solid growth at Disney but cost pressure at Warner Bros. and mixed signals at smaller players. Gaming & Lottery combines strong top‑line growth at Bally's with losses at Caesars and tightening spend at Light & Wonder. Publishing & Information balances AI investments at Wolters Kluwer with a revenue miss at Scholastic. Education sees Pearson’s growth, community‑focused data‑center work at NYU and cost cuts at SLU.

industries.summary: Disney posted 8% revenue growth and AI‑driven platform upgrades. Warner Bros. shows modest margin and cost‑cutting, while smaller firms lack clear guidance.

leaders.why: 8% revenue growth and AI platform launches

laggards.why: No financial data and neutral sentiment

themes.title: AI & tech investment
themes.detail: Disney launched AI search summaries and a trip‑planning tool; Wolters Kluwer added AI decision‑support tools.

themes.title: Digital rebuild
themes.detail: Hulu app retirement, Fandango platform lift, and FAST channel additions reshape content delivery.

themes.title: M&A & restructuring
themes.detail: Warner Bros. and Paramount studios merged; CBS staff buyouts signal cost focus.

industries.it_note: Disney is expanding IT spend on AI, while Warner Bros. tightens; overall outlook varies across players.

industries.summary: Bally's revenue surged 21.7% YoY, but Caesars posted a widened net loss. Light & Wonder tightens spend to reduce debt.

leaders.why: 21.7% YoY revenue growth driven by Intralot B2C

laggards.why: Widened $123 m net loss despite revenue growth

themes.title: Digital revenue growth
themes.detail: Caesars sees digital EBITDA rise and 5% digital revenue increase.

themes.title: Cost‑cutting & debt reduction
themes.detail: Light & Wonder prioritises debt reduction; Bally's refinances debt to improve liquidity.

themes.title: AI support claims
themes.detail: Caesars’ CEO says AI will support in‑person meetings, indicating cautious tech adoption.

industries.it_note: Bally's expands IT for integration, while Light & Wonder tightens spend; overall tech spend is uneven.

industries.summary: Wolters Kluwer expands AI tools, Scholastic misses revenue targets, and Pearson shows accelerated growth with AI credentialing.

leaders.why: Accelerated revenue growth and expanding AI credential platform

laggards.why: Revenue miss and widening operating loss

themes.title: AI & tech investment
themes.detail: Wolters Kluwer acquires AgileMD and launches Blue Chip IQ; Pearson’s Credly platform hits 150 m credentials.

themes.title: Revenue pressure
themes.detail: Scholastic reports a $216.8 m miss and negative margin.

industries.it_note: Both Wolters Kluwer and Pearson are increasing IT spend on AI and digital credentialing.

industries.summary: Pearson grows revenue, NYU focuses on community data‑center expectations, while SLU cuts custodial staff.

leaders.why: Revenue growth and expanding AI credentialing

laggards.why: Outsourced custodial services and laid off all staff

themes.title: AI credentialing

themes.title: Community data‑center focus
